input: Research accessible hiking trails for wheelchair users

gold.taskDescription: Find and evaluate hiking trails that are suitable and accessible for wheelchair users.

questions.title: What geographic area or region are you targeting?
questions.description: Identify the specific location, city, region, or country where the trails should be located.

questions.title: Who is the wheelchair user you are researching for?
questions.description: Clarify whether this is for yourself, a family member, a friend, or a group.

questions.title: What type of wheelchair is being used?
questions.description: Determine whether it is a manual wheelchair, power wheelchair, or all-terrain mobility device, as this affects trail suitability.

questions.title: What trail length or duration is ideal?
questions.description: Understand the preferred distance or time commitment for the hike, such as under 1 mile or half-day trips.

questions.title: Is there a preferred terrain type or scenery?
questions.description: Find out if the user prefers specific environments such as forests, lakesides, mountains, or coastal paths.

questions.title: Are there specific accessibility features that are required?
questions.description: Identify must-have features such as paved surfaces, rest areas, accessible restrooms, or parking.

questions.title: When are you planning to go on this hike?
questions.description: Establish the intended timeframe, as seasonal conditions or trail closures may affect availability and accessibility.
